An announcement was made, a first warning, two more strikes and they were out. For now, they would play on but not until the pitch was clear.Ballboys dashed across, applauded all the way, to do what ballboys do:pick up the balls. Planes were pushed off the pitch. Players kicked about among themselves. And, after a pause of eight minutes and 43 seconds, Sánchez Martínez, satisfied now, sent them back over to take the corner, Pathé Ciss congratulating a ballboy on a job well done as he returned to his position. The corner came in, Yuri Berchiche volleyed just wide, shot flashing past the post, and then the planes came down again. Two touches, strike two. This time, the referee took them off. The stadium clock had rolled on but now it was reset as they headed down the tunnel to chants of “Presa, go now!”They had been out there 24 minutes and 56 seconds but it might as well have been half-time. In the shadows of the narrow corridor under the stand, conversations unfolded. In the sunshine, so did the tinfoil, supporters happily eating the sandwiches meant for the break. Half an hour after kick-off, there was an announcement: they would begin again in 20 minutes. And if more objects are thrown, the match would be abandoned. From the tunnel, Isi Palazón and Óscar Valentíncame out to speak to fans behind the goal. This wasbad: if it happens again, the game is over. This wasgood, a plan forming: if it happens again, the game is over. A clear protocol, postponement easily forced, a statement made more visible, more powerful than ever before.View image in fullscreenRayo supporters protest with a banner that reads ‘Presa, go now’.Photograph: Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesThirty-eight minutes and 16 seconds after kick-off, the players reappeared, Athletic first. Sánchez Martínez bounced the ball, said it is flat, swapped it over, and gave it to Emil Audero, whose goal-kick would be the new kick-off, 43 minutes since the first time. From behind him, someone started a countdown:five, four, three …As the ball flew into the air, so did more paper planes. Sánchez Martínez shrugged, looked at the end, a hint of defiance. Leaning against his post at the other end,Unai Simón watched it all happen.Sánchez Martínez called over the captains, then the coaches. A circle formed on the pitch: the referee, his assistant, two captains, two managers, a delegate, La Liga’s match director, the security adviser and a police officer. The Rayo coach, Beñat San José, translated for Edin Terzic, whispering in his ear. Terzic nodded. Álvaro García argued, but there was nothing he could do. The referee’s hands were tied, the police wanted to go, and at nine minutes to three, 49 minutes and 18 seconds after the game started, he signalled towards the tunnel. They had played 13 minutes.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionRayo’s players departed, Ivan Balliu first, to applause. The referee stood, hands on his hips, a disapproving parent who had sent the kids to their room. Athletic’s players went to their fans in the far corner, then back towards Rayo’s supporters, who chanted: “Athletic! Athletic!”Iñaki Williams andSimón werethe last off. They stopped for photos with the ballboys. Williams gave someone his shirt, Simón handed over his gloves. As they reached the tunnel, Williams signed someone’s shirt. As they disappeared, the stadium launched into the Vida Pirata, usually a victory song.View image in fullscreenAthletic players wait on the pitch (left) as the referee makes the decision to abandon the match (right).Photograph: Florencia Tan Jun/Getty ImagesThey may not have won, may never win, but many wonder what they had left to lose. They were not planning to get it postponed, an opportunity opening instead, but they might next time. Presa says he will never leave, even if they fall to the third tier, but what if they do it again and again? At what point does someone step in?The club attack the “ultras”– that old get-out clause – and call the rest of the ground “victims”, but that is not how the rest of the ground sees it, flying their paper planes and happily heading off into the afternoon. Even Athletic’s supporters, their big day out brought to an early end, were on side. They joined Rayo fans in the bars while down in the offices, there were negotiations over when to replay the game, probably behind closed doors: Athletic wanted to return the following morning but that was rejected and so at 4.23pm on Saturday their bus pulled out for Barajas, applauded up Payaso Fofo street and right on to Avenida Albufera, still none the wiser.Quick GuideLa Liga resultsShowMálaga 1-1 Espanyol, Rayo 0-0 Athletic (abandoned), Alavés 1-2 Atlético Madrid, Barcelona 3-0 Getafe, Real Madrid 1-0 Villarreal, Elche 0-0 Celta, Real Sociedad 3-2 Deportivo, Betis 5-2 Osasuna, Racing Santander 2-2 ValenciaMonday:Levante v Sevilla (8pm BST)Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Rayo’s supporters’ association called this “the inevitable consequence of exhaustion, frustration and anger” after “15 years of abandonment of the facilities, chaotic management, a loss of identity and a continuous contempt for employees and fans, as well as the club and its values”. They called Presa “dictatorial”; the protest, by contrast, “peaceful and democratic, necessary”.“An unsustainable situation has reached its limit,” thecaptain Valentín posts. “This has got worse and worse bit by bit for too long without anyone doing anything to stop it getting this far. We have to listen to and understand the fans’ discontent. We need to find a way to bring everyone together for the common good and the good of Rayo Vallecano above all. That’s the only way we will ever live great moments together again.”PosTeamPGDPts1Barcelona827242Atletico Madrid810193Real Betis85194Real Madrid811185Sevilla71136Real Sociedad8-3137Alaves84118Deportivo A Coruna81109Celta Vigo82810Athletic Bilbao61811Villarreal80812Espanyol80813Rayo Vallecano7-5814Getafe8-6815Racing Santander8-10816Osasuna8-10817Elche8-6618Levante6-4519Valencia8-9520Malaga8-94Explore more on these topicsLa LigaRayo VallecanoEuropean club footballAthletic BilbaofeaturesShareReuse this content

title: The Deshaun Watson revival derailed, much to the joy of those with a functional memory | NFL | The Guardian
description: After three straight game-winning drives, Cleveland’s quarterback was sacked eight times in a dismal defeat that punctured the hype surrounding him
Author: Dave Schilling
Headline: After three straight game-winning drives, Cleveland’s quarterback was sacked eight times in a dismal defeat that punctured the hype surrounding him
Content: Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson is sacked by Jets cornerback Jarvis Brownlee Jr during the second half of Sunday’s game in East Rutherford, New Jersey.Photograph: Adam Hunger/APView image in fullscreenBrowns quarterback Deshaun Watson is sacked by Jets cornerback Jarvis Brownlee Jr during the second half of Sunday’s game in East Rutherford, New Jersey.Photograph: Adam Hunger/APNFLThe Deshaun Watson revival derailed, much to the joy of those with a functional memoryAfter three straight game-winning drives, Cleveland’s quarterback was sacked eight times in a dismal defeat that punctured the hype surrounding himDave SchillingMon 12 Oct 2026 03.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 12 Oct 2026 07.42 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIguess the New York Jets didn’t get the memo. This was supposed to be a Deshaun Watson lovefest. A day where, much to the chagrin of those of us witha moral compass and a functional memory, football fans worldwide could declare Watson was “so back” and that the Browns were in some blinkered, alternate universe, a Super Bowl contender. No such luck, as the Browns looked like the Browns – reminding an otherwise jubilant city of Cleveland that they are trapped in the sports equivalent of the Backrooms.Limping along for 155 passing yards and one touchdown, Watson fell to Earth harder than David Bowie in a Nicolas Roeg film (yes, I just watched the Dennis Miller Monday Night Football documentary on HBO). He completed fewer than 50% of his passes and ended the day with a 69.6 passer rating. I should also probably mention he got sacked eight times. Yes, eight times.EIGHT TIMES. He only completed seven more passes than he received punishing hits behind the line of scrimmage. It was a performance NBC NFL writer Patrick Daugherty called “unspeakably bad.” Actually, I think the performance was very much speakable, as I’ve demonstrated here. Stick around for another 400 words.NFL roundup: Daniels’ overtime blunder costs Commanders as Giants salvage wild 27-27 tieRead moreThe thing that has defined Watson’s run as a potentially viableNFLquarterback has been his ability to march down the field and win a game in the dying embers of the contest. After three game-winning drives to start the season, it seemed like the Browns were poised to pull out another improbable victory from deep where the sun don’t shine, but no. Not today.On fourth and 11 – with less than a minute left in the fourth quarter, down by five –Watson dropped back, only for his pocket to evaporate faster than a spilled Dasani in the middle of the Mojave Desert. Ejected violently from the pocket, Watson begins to scramble. On fourth and 11, by the way. He’s unceremoniously tackled near the line of scrimmage, putting the game on ice.Starting off Sunday, these seemed like two teams going in the opposite direction, but the reality on the field was more like the Spider-Man pointing meme. Offensive ineptitude, with both the Jets and Browns recording fewer than 300 yards of total offense, giving away two fumbles, and failing to convert touchdowns twice in the red zone. The New York Post might havecalled this game “tense” and “gritty”, but I’m sure many viewers could think of more apropos adjectives to describe what they witnessed – a game that hinged on a botched snap sailing through the hands of Browns punter Corey Bojorquez. That wayward punt turned into a game-winning touchdown for Jets RB Braelon Allen.This loss, dropping Cleveland to 3-2 on the year, felt like a necessary corrective to the hyperbole andearly extension talksaround Watson’s early successes. American sports fans love a comeback story, but this one is mired inissues that are far more important than football. It certainly makes everyone’s life easier when he plays like this.MVP of the weekCam Little, K, Jacksonville Jaguars. Sure, there’s probably more splashy statistical performances from today. You could make a strong case for Drake Maye, whose 374 yards and four touchdowns gave the Patriots a resounding win over the Raiders. But I’m not going to do that, because we ride for placekickers when I’m around. In a bleak, dystopian ending that felt more like the final five minutes of Digger than a football game, the Eagles went up 17-16 with a mere eight seconds left in the contest. Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni, misplacing his copy of Football for Dummies, decided to have his kicker boot the ball in play rather than ice it with a touchback. A 53-yard return by Ameer Abdullah perfectly set up a gargantuan field goal to win the game for the Jags.View image in fullscreenJaguars kicker Cam Little celebrates after kicking the winning field goal against the Eagles in London on Sunday.Photograph: Ian Walton/AP“I didn’t make the right decision, and I lost us that game, and that’s what I said to our guys,” Siriannitold the mediaafter Christmas came early in London for Jacksonville. Now, a 57-yard field goal with nearly no time left on the clock isn’t exactly a gimme. One could maybe forgive Sirianni for thinking the chances of a field goal from distance to steal the game was unlikely. Except, the Jaguars’ kicker is Little – the man who holds the record for the longest made field goal in NFL history. A recordhe set almost a full year ago. The Eagles gave Little a dagger. He should be commended for knowing how to use it.Video of the weekThe Texans won their first game of the year, demolishing an equally troubled, still-winless Titans team 26-3. CJ Stroud dropped 261 yards, a passing touchdown, and a running touchdown on Tennessee, cementing a bounce-back moment that has the NFL buzzing about just how much money he’ll command on the free-agent market. More importantly, today’s result is coupled with news of Houston getting Stroud reinforcements. WR Marvin Harrison is on the way to the Texans from the Cardinals and Houston coach DeMeco Ryans was more than happy to officially drop the bomb in a brief post-game presser:Allow content provided by a third party?This article includes content hosted onplatform.x.com. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as the provider may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content,click 'Allow and continue'.Allow and continueBrevity really is the soul of wit.Stat of the weekBefore their drubbing by the Patriots, the Raiders had scored at least 26 points in all four of their games this season. Here, they didn’t score more than a touchdown until the fourth quarter, managing a meager 17 points on the road at Gillette Stadium. Las Vegas had a chance to keep pace with the AFC West leading Chiefs during KC’s bye week, but Kirk Cousins was sacked three times and couldn’t convert scoring opportunities into touchdowns. Cousins was replaced by rookie Fernando Mendoza in garbage time, showing how thoroughly the Raiders were handled. They certainly didn’t benefit from giving up 165 rushing yards, spread across multiple New England players (including 25 yards on the ground for Maye). The Pats grabbed 8.1 yards per play, as efficient and deadly as it gets.Elsewhere around the leagueAfter a World Cup in North America, I hope everyone here has gotten used to the concept of a tie. The Giants and Commanders certainly have. In an example of hopeless, foggy-eyed game management, Washington blew a chance to win the game in overtime. A Cam Skattebo turnover handed the Commanders the ball with enough time for Jayden Daniels to march down to the New York 24-yard line. A luxurious 12 seconds remained on the clock. More than enough time to plunk in a field goal to win it. Except, the Commanders wandered around the line of scrimmage for exactly 12 seconds and never did snap the ball, let alone spike it to stop the clock to set up for a kick. Commanders coach Dan Quinn, like Sirianni in the Eagles-Jags game,took the blame for the mistake. For once, I’d like to see a coach just completely throw his players under the bus. “Hey man, I’m not playing. Don’t look at me.” Just for variety.Put the phone down. No need to call the authorities on your friends who are Steelers fans. After a game withvisible tension between Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthyon Thursday Night Football on 1 October, the ship was righted in Steel City, USA. Rodgers looked tidy and comfortable, connecting in the end zone with Pat Freiermuth twice to defeat the Colts 34-22.The Vikings are still undefeated, dropping the Saints to 1-4 on the year. The game was not as close as the 23-13 score, with Minnesota dominating every major team category. New Orleans finished with a paltry 142 total yards. Only 55 of those came on the ground. The Saints only recorded one offensive touchdown, with the other coming on a fumble recovery. The story was far different for the Vikes. Minnesota RB Aaron Jones gobbled up 113 yards and one touchdown in front of moribund Saints fans in the Superdome. Kyler Murray benefitted greatly from Justin Jefferson’s return to action, throwing for 229 yards and a touchdown. Can anyone beat this Vikings team? They’ve got a bye in week six, then the 2-3 Colts, back at US Bank Stadium. That doesn’t seem promising for Indy.View image in fullscreenVikings running back Aaron Jones Sr is congratulated by teammates after scoring a touchdown during Sunday’s 23-13 victory over the Saints in New Orleans.Photograph: Gerald Herbert/APThe winless Dolphins almost pulled off a last-second miracle against the Bengals, getting within a touchdown with less than a minute left in the game. But kicker Riley Patterson missed the extra point before an onside kick attempt to recover possession was unsuccessful. Cincinnati took the win 31-24 off a splashy four-touchdown day for Joe Burrow. Can anyone lose to this Dolphins team? They’ve got a bye in week six, then the 2-3 Jets, on the road at MetLife Stadium. That doesn’t seem promising for viewers.The NFL’s oldest rivalry continued, with the Packers tossing the Bears in a meat freezer and locking the door. Green Bay danced away with the win in the teams’ 214th ever matchup (including playoffs), 31-7. Caleb Williams, perhaps the most hated man in Wisconsin after his ruthless comeback win against Green Bay in last year’s playoffs, remained out. In his stead, Tyson Bagent looked worse than anyone could have imagined, 12-of-21 for 87 yards and two interceptions before being benched for Case Keenum. At most, Bears coach Ben Johnson would say that Williams is “on track” to return, but with no definitive date set. NFL reporter Ian Rappaport did suggest that there’s a chance he can play in week six against the Atlanta Falcons. Perhaps the Chicago faithful shouldplace a call to Pope Leo to speed this thing along.As a Rams fan still smarting fromour disastrous Australian drubbing, the last thing I want to talk about is the 49ers looking like the class of the entire NFL. But San Francisco’s trip to Lumen Field to face Seattle might have been the most consequential matchup of week five. The NFC West has three legitimate Super Bowl contenders (and the Cardinals), and two of them faced off here on Sunday. Seattle and San Francisco traded punches all day, but the game came down to rare, crucial mistakes, as matchups between good teams often do.Sam Darnold threw two pivotal interceptions, RB George Holani fumbled right before halftime, leading to a touchdown that put the 49ers up by eight. Seattle exploded for a touchdown and two field goals in the third, tilting the scales back in their direction. But a seven-yard TD pass from Brock Purdy to Brandin Cooks flipped the script yet again. A successful two-point conversion gave the Niners a three-point lead. Seattle kicker Jason Myers tied it up with a little under seven minutes to play, but the Seahawks couldn’t get a stop to force overtime. A 44-yard Eddy Pineiro field goal gave the 49ers a slim advantage. Darnold linked with WR Cooper Kupp, who just nearly converted a fourth-and 10 at the 50, which would have given Seattle one last crack at the ballgame. But a controversial spot of the ball left Kupp short and handed San Francisco their fifth win of 2026. And they did it without ace receiver Deebo Samuel, who left the game in the third quarter with a hamstring injury. Niners fans hold their breath. And I put another pin in the voodoo doll.Explore more on these topicsNFLCleveland BrownsUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Renshaw’s heroics leave South Africa reeling as Australia close on first Test victory | Cricket | The Guardian
description: Matt Renshaw followed up his epic first-innings 190 with an impressive 82, plus Temba Bavuma’s wicket, to put Australia on course for a statement win against South Africa in Durban
Author: Geoff Lemon
Headline: Matt Renshaw followed up his epic first-innings 190 with an impressive 82, plus Temba Bavuma’s wicket, to put Australia on course for a statement win against South Africa in Durban
Content: Matt Renshaw worked more magic with bat and ball to put Australia on course for a statement win in Durban.Photograph: Themba Hadebe/APView image in fullscreenMatt Renshaw worked more magic with bat and ball to put Australia on course for a statement win in Durban.Photograph: Themba Hadebe/APCricketRenshaw’s heroics leave South Africa reeling as Australia close on first Test victoryGeoff LemonMon 12 Oct 2026 12.25 EDTLast modified on Mon 12 Oct 2026 18.26 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWhat a few days it has been in the life of Matt Renshaw. His comeback to the Test team had consisted of one innings, edged to slip for eight, before he made the trip to South Africa, where his job as opener suddenly changed to batting five.His first two days of the first Test in Durban were spent compilinghis epic 190to rescue Australia. Then camehis fourth day, hammering in the nails on a declaration by top scoring again with 82. Pulling out at 316 for six, Australia set South Africa 421 to win, then took four wickets for 102 by the close; Aiden Markram on 45 will be the main obstacle to an Australian series lead on the final day.Georgia Voll’s quickfire century lifts Australia to ODI series win against BangladeshRead moreWhat stood out with Renshaw was the shift in styles. His first innings was one marked by calm and accumulation, building with minimal risk. His second, with a target to set, was dynamic, regularly sweeping and reverse-sweeping, flummoxing South Africa’s keeper and slip by shaping for the reverse. Kyle Verreynne was so distracted that he let through four byes, while Markram tried to emulate Steve Smith by running across at slip, only to watch Renshaw sweep it through the gap that Markram had just created.As Renshaw started hitting South Africa’s spinners for sixes, he was on track for the rare feat of twin centuries in a Test. It took an oddity to stop that, Keshav Maharaj fumbling the ball half a dozen times and accidentally bouncing it off his own head before holding a return catch prone on the pitch.A strike rate of 82 in the second innings compared to 47 in the first showed Renshaw’s range, and his match tally of 272 runs was near the record by an Australian against South Africa. He finished three runs behind Phillip Hughes, after twin tons at the same ground; eight behind David Warner’s two centuries in Cape Town in 2014; and 27 runs behind Donald Bradman’s famous 299 not out, when the No 11, Pud Thurlow, was run out trying to come back for a second.Nic Maddinson’s second innings was also a contrast to his first, following up his painful duck with 48 from 38 balls. Having thrown the bat for 17 not out the previous evening, he continued in the same vein despite Travis Head being caught off a leading edge for 11. Maddinson slashed three boundaries through the cordon, middled one through cover, and belted Simon Harmer for a straight six, before missing an equally straight yorker from Anrich Nortje, the opening bat’s back foot twitching out of the way as the low full toss arrived at pace.View image in fullscreenAiden Markram dives unsuccessfully in an attempt to catch Matt Renshaw.Photograph: Themba Hadebe/APHis scoring rate did give Australia impetus, which was consolidated by double-figure scores throughout the order. Smith was hit in the helmet by Nortje before going on his own hitting spree, holing out down the ground for 27, optimistically trying to hit Harmer over Marco Jansen twice in one over. Marnus Labuschagne made an identical score to his first innings, 37 from 58 balls, and looked good before driving a flighted Maharaj ball to cover for Temba Bavuma’s second catch. Nortje returned to have Alex Carey edge a drive into his stumps for 24.By then, though, the lead was 311, and it was a relative cruise as Renshaw extended it to 376 before the next pair iced the cake, Beau Webster with five fours and Pat Cummins with four sixes. The captain’s 32 from 12 balls was an emphatic end, as was declaring just before the tea break rather than bother with timing it to mess with South Africa’s openers.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every daySign up toAustralia SportGet a daily roundup of the latest sports news, features and comment from our Australian sports deskEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe more relaxed preparation worked for Australia initially, with Josh Hazlewood extending his hold over Ryan Rickelton by having him edge a pull to the keeper on two. As in the first innings, David Bedingham put together a solid stand with Markram, and as in the first innings, fell short of a half century, leg before to Hazlewood for 46.That was when the tone shifted. As if Renshaw’s match wasn’t already good enough, Cummins gave him a bowl late in the day, and he duly picked up Bavuma, the South African captain, at bat pad, at the same time opening the door for Cummins to have Tristan Stubbs nick a drive to Carey. At the close, South Africa needed 319 more runs, or more realistically to survive as much of the fifth day as bad light will allow. The way Renshaw lifted up Labuschagne in celebration of his first Test wicket might be symbolic; the returning player has done all he can to carry his reclaimed team to victory.Explore more on these topicsCricketAustralia cricket teamSouth Africa cricket teamAustralia sportmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: England split cricket coaching setups and hand out record 39 central contracts | England cricket team | The Guardian
description: Rob Key issues bumper number of central contracts and pledges to ‘map out’ next two years for England men’s teams
Author: Ali Martin
Headline: Rob Key issues bumper number of central contracts and pledges to ‘map out’ next two years for England men’s teams
Content: Ollie Robinson has earned a central contract after a remarkable return to international cricket this summer.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianView image in fullscreenOllie Robinson has earned a central contract after a remarkable return to international cricket this summer.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianEngland cricket teamEngland split cricket coaching setups and hand out record 39 central contractsRobinson, Duckett and Smith get one-year dealsEric Simons hired as Test fast-bowling coachAli MartinMon 12 Oct 2026 08.31 EDTLast modified on Mon 12 Oct 2026 12.32 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRob Key believes he can now “map out the next two years” for the England men’s teams, having handed out a record 39 central contracts and unveiled new split coaching setups under Stephen Fleming andBrendon McCullumthat he hopes will produce homegrown candidates for the top roles in future.Theretirements of Ben Stokesand Mark Wood, plus Zak Crawley being dropped, have allowed Key, the England team director, to stretch the pot of money for player contracts further this year. Thirty main deals have been issued – up from 26 last year – while nine players have been handed development contracts that top up their county pay.‘Franchise cricket isn’t as rewarding’: Jonathan Trott on Lions pride and England ambitionsRead moreThere is a blend of one- and two-year contracts in the main group, with Joe Root,Harry Brook, Jofra Archer and Jacob Bethell extending terms until the end of 2028. Jordan Cox, a bright spark from the summer, jumps straight into the two-year list, as do two rookie fast bowlers: Sonny Baker has seven caps across all formats, Henry Crocombe is uncapped. The all-rounders Sam Curran and Will Jacks also get two-year deals.But Key is also keen to keep others hungry, with Ben Duckett and Jamie Smith kept to 12 months apiece – a sign of needing to bolt down their Test spots – likewise Ollie Robinson after hisremarkable return during the summer. Emilio Gay and Dan Lawrence also get one-year deals, as does Ollie Pope, despite being frozen out of the England XI since midway through last winter’s Ashes.Asked about Duckett and Smith specifically, Key replied: “Yeah, we debated and deliberated long and hard about those types of things. We feel that this is going to be the thing that gets the best out of those guys.“In a few other cases, they’re just a longer-term bet. You want to make sure you can almost map out the next two years.”Beyond what is now a super-sized squad that covers all formats – and allows continued control of workloads, albeit with established windows for the Indian Premier League and the Hundred – the coaching teams are settled before Fleming starts his new role as Test head coach in South Africa this winter.Quick GuideEngland men's central contracts: the full listShowTwo-year contracts (to Sep 2028):Joe Root (Yorkshire), Harry Brook (Yorkshire), Jofra Archer (Sussex), Gus Atkinson (Surrey), Sonny Baker (Hampshire), Jacob Bethell (Warwickshire), Jordan Cox (Essex), Henry Crocombe (Sussex/Surrey), Sam Curran* (Surrey), Will Jacks (Surrey), Josh Tongue (Nottinghamshire).One-year contracts (to Sep 2027):Rehan Ahmed (Leicestershire), Tom Banton (Somerset), Shoaib Bashir (Derbyshire), Jos Buttler (Lancashire), Brydon Carse (Durham), Sam Cook (Essex), Liam Dawson (Hampshire), Ben Duckett (Nottinghamshire), Emilio Gay (Durham), Matthew Fisher (Surrey), Dan Lawrence (Surrey), Saqib Mahmood (Lancashire), Jamie Overton (Surrey), Ollie Pope (Surrey), Matthew Potts (Durham), Adil Rashid (Yorkshire), Ollie Robinson (Sussex), Phil Salt (Lancashire), Jamie Smith (Surrey)Development contracted players 2026–27:James Coles (Sussex), Mason Crane (Glamorgan), Josh Hull (Leicestershire), Eddie Jack (Hampshire), Ben McKinney (Durham), Liam Patterson-White (Nottinghamshire), Thomas Rew (Somerset), Matthew Revis (Yorkshire), Mitch Stanley (Lancashire)Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Marcus Trescothick will remain as an assistant coach to the Test side only and in come James Foster and Richard Dawson. Dawson has also been named as “national spin-bowling lead” and will leave his current role at Glamorgan, with Key praising his work at one of the less well-resourced counties.The South African Eric Simons, an ally of Fleming at Chennai Super Kings and once described as “the best in the world” by Stokes, has been hired as the Test fast-bowling coach. It ends a run of short-term hires when McCullum was Test head coach, including Jimmy Anderson, David Saker and Tim Southee.Southee and Jeetan Patel will now solely be part of McCullum’s white-ball staff to give it a strong New Zealand flavour, with Sarah Taylor the one full-time English coach here. Kevin Pietersen will continue to make guest appearances as a “specialist mentor” as Brook’s side looks to the 2027 World Cup.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe SpinSubscribe to our cricket newsletter for our writers' thoughts on the biggest stories and a review of the week’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBut with Jonathan Trott now in charge of the Lions and Mike Yardy promoted to an overarching role as “national batting lead” after a summer spent working with the Test side and past experience with the under-19s, Key sees future head coach candidates emerging from the English game.“We’ve got the best of what this country has to offer,” said Key. “There is part of a succession plan in there that may or may not happen because you never know what happens in these jobs. But I certainly think there’s a number of coaches that have the potential not only to learn, but go and do the [head coach] job in the future. Richard Dawson would be near the top of that list.”Before any such vacancy emerges, Dawson will first need to address England’s longstanding issues in the spin department. Shoaib Bashir gets another one-year deal, despite not featuring during the Ashes or against Pakistan, while Mason Crane and Liam Patterson-White receive development deals. Patterson-White, a left-arm finger spinner, may well signpost plans for the Test tour of Bangladesh in February.The fast bowler Brydon Carse goes into the second year of his existing central contract while undergoing a disciplinary with theCricketRegulator after his brief arrest in Derby in August. Key said he will let the process run its course but doesn’t “see anything to suggest” that Carse will have his England deal ended prematurely.Explore more on these topicsEngland cricket teamCricketJoe RootHarry BrookBrendon McCullumnewsShareReuse this content

title: Saudi Arabia further suspends flights after latest deadly Houthi attack on airport | Saudi Arabia | The Guardian
description: Energy minister says ‘fear has no place in the Saudi lexicon’ as paramilitary group again breaches stretched defences
Author: Patrick Wintour
Headline: Energy minister says ‘fear has no place in the Saudi lexicon’ as paramilitary group again breaches stretched defences
Content: 0:44CCTV from inside Riyadh airport shows moment of deadly airstrike – videoSaudi ArabiaSaudi Arabia further suspends flights after latest deadly Houthi attack on airportEnergy minister says ‘fear has no place in the Saudi lexicon’ as paramilitary group again breaches stretched defencesWhy are the Houthis attacking Saudi airports and how are the missiles getting through?Patrick WintourDiplomatic editorMon 12 Oct 2026 11.42 EDTFirst published on Mon 12 Oct 2026 07.49 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSaudi Arabia has been forced to suspend all flights to and from its main international airport in Riyadh until next Saturday after afurther round of Houthi missile attackscaused more damage and left one person dead. Some airlines, including Gulf Air and Bahrain Air, had already said they were cancelling flights until next Saturday. More missiles were fired at Saudi Arabian cities by the Houthis on Monday, Saudi Arabian’s military spokesperson said.The Gulf nation announced it was suspending flights from Riyadh, its second busiest airport, after Houthi missileskilled 13 people on Saturdayand left more than 300 injured. Saudi state TV broadcast CCTV footage that showed passengers deluged in smoke and falling masonry as they queued at the airport terminal to board a plane just as the Houthi missile struck.View image in fullscreenBefore and after the strike as people queue up for flights at King Khalid international airport on Saturday.Photograph: Saudi Ministry of Media/ReutersThe country has pressed ahead with the 25th WPC Energy Conference in Riyadh, hoping to project an image of normality. But some senior oil executives did not attend or appeared virtually.The Saudi energy minister, Abdulaziz bin Salman, told the conference that “fear has no place in the Saudi lexicon”, emphasising the resilience of the kingdom’s energy system and the determination of its people to confront crises. Amin Nasser, the president and chief executive of Aramco, saidSaudi Arabiahad invested deeply in protecting its supplies, but “no nation, even one as capable and confident as ours, can safeguard them alone.”He added: “Markets can diversify suppliers. They cannot diversify geography […] when energy infrastructure in this region is targeted, the consequences reach economies everywhere.”An urgent review is under way as to how Houthi missiles are repeatedly penetrating badly stretched Saudi air defences. Schoolchildren and some office workers were advised to work from home. TheHouthishave also targeted the city of Khamis Mushait, and the King Fahd international airport in Dammam.Interceptor missiles are needed to protect government buildings, oil facilities and infrastructure hubs across a wide geographic area. The Houthis have vowed to attack Saudi airports across the country.A Houthi official on Monday warned the US it would receive a “painful response” if it entered the war inYemen, following Trump’s comments at the weekend that he was “going to look at” the possibility of joining Saudi strikes.“If the US becomes involved in the aggression against Yemen, we will not deliberate over the decision to respond, rather, there will be a swift and painful response targeting the US and all its interests in the region,” Houthi political bureau member Mohammed Al Bukhaiti told AFP in an interview.He also warned “all employees and workers at Saudi oil facilities and airports to stay away from these sites, as they have become legitimate targets”.Houthi attacks since last month have targeted fuel tanks at Riyadh airport and its affiliated warehouses, destroying a parked Airbus A320 passenger plane and damaging at least five other aircraft.The crown prince, Mohammed bin Salman, has not been seen in public since Tuesday last week, reflecting the pressure he is under to find a way out from a war that has intermittently dogged his leadership since 2014. Saudi Arabia badly needs stability to continue the slow diversification of its economy from oil dependence, but has not found a way to restore it in Yemen.Inside Yemen, fighting continued in and around Taiz, the third city, and the most populous governorate, with Saudi planes mounting eight separate strikes on any assembly of Houthi forces. As many as 60 fighters died on Sunday from both sides.The governor of Taiz, Nabil Shamsan, on Sunday issued an urgent call to lift the Houthi siege and warned a shortage of medicines meant the city would soon run out of emergency surgical and intensive care services.Overall the Houthis claimed the Saudis had mounted 124 raids on Sunday. The Saudis are seeking to locate Abdul-Malik al-Houthi, the reclusive leader of the Houthis, with rumours of his assassination repeatedly circulating, but Saudi Arabia does not seem to have contemporary intelligence on his precise whereabouts either in the capital Sana’a or in its stronghold of Saada.View image in fullscreenA billboard displays an image of the Houthi leader, Abdul-Malik al-Houthi, in Sana’a, Yemen on Sunday.Photograph: Yahya Arhab/EPAOn the diplomatic front, Abbas Araghchi, the Iranian foreign minister, spoke to the Saudi foreign minister, Faisal bin Farhan, on Sunday to see if there was a way in which Iran could act as a mediator between the Saudis and the Houthis, a group that Iran has trained and armed. Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, a member of the Houthi Political Bureau claimed Saudi Arabia accepted the mediation offered by Iran and proposed first a one-month truce, and then a two week truce, but the Houthis had rejected both offers.He said “the battle this time is not like its predecessors; the arena is no longer the same arena, and the cards have changed. Therefore, a comprehensive settlement must be put in place between Riyadh and Sana’a, the Houthi capital because every day that passes in this battle will expand its scope and deepen its losses, and the settlement that is possible today may become difficult or impossible tomorrow”.A meeting of the UN security council in New York on Tuesday is expected to debate a resolution calling the Houthis a foreign terrorist organisation.The exiled leader of the Southern Transitional Council (STC), Aidarous al-Zubaidi, called for southern forces to fight on all fronts, and not just to defend the borders of the former South Yemen, in a move that is likely to be welcomed by Saudi Arabia as it supports the week-old call by the UN-recognised government to drive the Houthis out of the whole of Yemen, rather than just from the southern governorates.The Gulf has entered a new era of instability. If its leaders think they can rely on old alliances, they are wrong | Nesrine MalikRead moreThe STC has a vision of an independent South Yemen that would recreate the separate state that existed between 1967 and 1990. The reunification of Yemen at the end of the cold war proved fragile and many southerners nurse longstanding grievances about the distribution of resources in the unified state.The STC’s authority has been challenged by Abd al-Rahman al-Mahrami, the Salafist leader who commands the powerful Southern Giants Brigades.Despite Araghchi’s efforts to reach out to the Saudis, Mohsen Rezaei, the more hardline secretary of Iran’s supreme national security council, claimed Iran was hitting five or six small vessels in the strait of Hormuz every night, explaining the vessels were being used by the Emirati military to move oil through the strait to larger tankers, thus breaching the blockade that Iran is seeking to maintain to push up oil prices and weakenDonald Trump.Esmail Baghaei, the Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson, said Trump’s treatment of Volodymyr Zelenskyy, includinghis call for the Ukrainian president to stand asideshowed the risks in dealing with Trump. He said: “Being an enemy of America can be dangerous, but being a friend of America is deadly. You can see for yourself what America’s friendship and enmity with its allies is like.”Explore more on these topicsSaudi ArabiaHouthisVolodymyr ZelenskyyUkraineYemenMiddle East and north AfricaDonald TrumpnewsShareReuse this content

title: Selma Blair arrested at JFK after she allegedly attacked flight attendants | Selma Blair | The Guardian
description: Several news outlets reported Blair allegedly punched a flight attendant, bit another and tried to open plane door
Author: Maya Yang
Headline: Several news outlets reported Blair allegedly punched a flight attendant, bit another and tried to open plane door
Content: Actor Selma Blair attends Variety’s 2026 Power of Women: Los Angeles event in Beverly Hills, California, on 23 September.Photograph: Mario Anzuoni/ReutersView image in fullscreenActor Selma Blair attends Variety’s 2026 Power of Women: Los Angeles event in Beverly Hills, California, on 23 September.Photograph: Mario Anzuoni/ReutersSelma BlairSelma Blair arrested at JFK after she allegedly attacked flight attendantsSeveral news outlets reported Blair allegedly punched a flight attendant, bit another and tried to open plane doorMaya Yangin New YorkMon 12 Oct 2026 16.03 EDTLast modified on Mon 12 Oct 2026 18.45 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe actorSelma Blairwas arrested on Sunday at John F Kennedy (JFK) airport inNew Yorkon allegations that she attacked flight attendants on a Delta Air Lines flight, according to officials.Blair’s arrest happened at about 11pm, after Port Authority ofNew Yorkand New Jersey officials said they responded to a call “about a physically abusive passenger aboard Delta Air Lines flight 938 which was parked at the gate” at JFK after arriving from Los Angeles (LAX).Blair, 54, “was taken into custody and transported to the hospital for evaluation”, the port authority also said on Monday. “Two flight attendants also reported injuries, and one was transported to the hospital for further evaluation.”The port authority said the FBI – which handles reports of crimes on airplanes – was investigating Sunday’s allegations against Blair.Asked to comment on Blair’s arrest, a Delta spokesperson said the airline “has zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behavior, as the safety of our customers and crew always comes first”.The spokesperson added that Blair’s arrest did not affect the flight she and her fellow passengers were on – and that it still landed ahead of schedule at JFK.Several news outlets on Mondayreportedthat Blair allegedly punched a flight attendant, bit another and tried to open the airplane door.Statements released by officials did not immediately address those reported details.But an air traffic control audio recording from the flight Blair was on captured the pilot saying “one flight attendant and one passenger … sustained some minor injuries – a bloody nose as well as some bite marks”.“I don’t think we need an ambulance or anything like that – but we just want to get some medical personnel at the gate to look at their injuries,” the pilot said, according to the recording, a copy of which waspublishedby NBC Los Angeles.The flight controller replied that paramedics were approaching the gate – and that law enforcement was already there.The Guardian has reached out to Blair’s representatives for additional comment. Her publicisttoldthe Hollywood Reporter: “Selma experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct. Upon landing, she received immediate medical attention and is [now] in stable condition.”Sunday marked at least the second time Blair was reported to be involved in such an incident. In 2016, shereportedlybegan screaming uncontrollably before being removed on a stretcher while on a Los Angeles-bound flight from Cancún, Mexico.Blair apologized after the earlier episode, saying that she “mixed alcohol with medication”.“That caused me to black out and led me to say and do things that I deeply regret,” Blair said at the time.The actor has also made news headlines for a 2018multiple sclerosisdiagnosis. And in February 2024, sheapologizedfor an Islamophobic comment on social media.Blair’s starring film credits include Cruel Intentions, Legally Blonde and Hellboy. She earned a best spoken world album for children nomination at the 2011 Grammy awards, for her work on Anne Frank: The Diary of a Young Girl – The Definitive Edition.Explore more on these topicsSelma BlairNew YorkUS crimenewsShareReuse this content

title: Student lay in wait for housemate before stabbing him 30 times, Bristol court hears | UK news | The Guardian
description: Zack Coughlan is accused of murdering Jamie Collins, with whom he studied at the University of the West of England
Author: Steven Morris
Headline: Zack Coughlan is accused of murdering Jamie Collins, with whom he studied at the University of the West of England
Content: Jamie Collins was attacked on 8 April after returning  home from campus on his bike, Bristol crown court was told.Photograph: Family Handout/Avon and Somerset police/PAJamie Collins was attacked on 8 April after returning  home from campus on his bike, Bristol crown court was told.Photograph: Family Handout/Avon and Somerset police/PAUK newsStudent lay in wait for housemate before stabbing him 30 times, Bristol court hearsZack Coughlan is accused of murdering Jamie Collins, with whom he studied at the University of the West of EnglandSteven MorrisMon 12 Oct 2026 10.04 EDTLast modified on Mon 12 Oct 2026 16.11 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA university student lay in wait for his housemate to return home before stabbing him 30 times, a murder trial has been told.Zack Coughlan, 23, dressed in black and wore a mask and gloves to ambush Jamie Collins, 21, in the garden of their home near the University of West England in Bristol, where both were studying robotics.Collins was attacked shortly before 6pm on 8 April after returning from campus on his bike, Bristol crown court heard.Coughlan then allegedly cycled away on the bike, dumped it at a nearby retail park, bought a change of clothes and threw his bloodstained clothing into a pond.He returned to the house they shared in Filton, south Gloucestershire, at about 9pm, put a pizza in the oven and did some online gaming with friends, the court was told.Adam Vaitilingam KC, prosecuting, said: “A few hours later he decided it was time to call the police and pretend that he had just found his friend’s body in the garden.“At about 2am, eight hours later, the defendant called 999. He said that his friend had been stabbed. They told him to do CPR until paramedics arrived and he told them that he was.”He told police he had noticed the back gate was open, went outside and found Collins’s body.The court heard the attack was caught on CCTV installed at the house, which Coughlan showed officers, who initially treated him as a witness.Coughlan had injuries to his hands but he said he had hurt himself when he fell while climbing trees.Vaitilingam said that as the evidence against Coughlan mounted, he went from being a witness to a suspect. He now accepted he had killed Collins but denied murder. He said he “lost his self-control” when he carried out the attack, the barrister said.The jury was told that Coughlan and Collins were final-year students and lived together in a house owned by the defendant.Vaitilingam said there had been disagreements between the pair about rent and whether Coughlan was charging too much, but they appeared to have been resolved.“There was nothing that any friends were aware of that seemed to be a significant problem,” he said. “They hung out together, both in person and online, they did gaming together, they went out together; entirely normal student life.”The trial continues.Explore more on these topicsUK newsEnglandnewsShareReuse this content

title: NAZA: Netanyahu orders identification and prosecution of film’s interviewees | NAZA | The Guardian
description: Israeli PM calls for criminal investigation into soldiers and officers interviewed in Guardian-produced documentary
Author: Lorenzo Tondo
Headline: Israeli PM calls for criminal investigation into soldiers and officers interviewed in Guardian-produced documentary
Content: 1:55NAZA - official trailerNAZANAZA: Netanyahu orders identification and prosecution of film’s intervieweesIsraeli PM calls for criminal investigation into soldiers and officers interviewed in Guardian-produced documentaryLorenzo TondoMon 12 Oct 2026 08.59 EDTLast modified on Mon 12 Oct 2026 12.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has ordered the country’s attorney general and the head of the Shin Bet security service to reveal the identities of soldiers and officers interviewed in the investigative documentaryNAZAand prosecute them for causing “harm to Israel’s diplomatic and security interests”.The award-winning documentary, directed by the Oscar-winning film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor and produced by the Guardian, details Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza. The film is in cinemas, including in the UK and the US, and will be shown in more than 50 countries.In a letter addressed to the attorney general, Gali Baharav-Miara, the IDF chief of staff, Lt Gen Eyal Zamir, and the Shin Bet head, David Zini,the Israeli prime minister demandedthey “act urgently to uncover the identity of all those who are involved or appear in the libel film”.Netanyahu also called for “the opening of a criminal investigation and prosecution for serious information security offences, criminal defamation, and harming Israel’s diplomatic and security interests”.NAZA premiered last month at the Venice international film festival, where itwon the special jury prizeafter receiving the longest ovation in the event’s history. It takes its name from an acronym used euphemistically by Israeli intelligence to indicatehow many civilians it expects to be killed in an airstrike.View image in fullscreenNAZA’s directors, Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, won the special jury prize at the Venice film festival last month.Photograph: Capital Pictures/Alamy Stock Photo/Alamy Live News.The Israeli government has fiercely attacked Abraham and Szor,threatening to strip them of their citizenshipand accusing them of treason. Government supporters have vowed to hound the film-makers on their return to Israel and picketed Szor’s parents’ home in Savyon, chanting: “Death sentence to traitors.”Zamir denounced the film as an “attack on the state of Israel”, accusing it ofspreading “lies and blood libels”. He had earlier ordered military and legal officials to identify the soldiers featured and examine possible legal action against them. However, the military advocate general, Itai Ofir, said criminal prosecution would require evidence of security violations or disclosure of classified material, although disciplinary measures remained possible.The protection of journalistic sources is a cornerstone of press freedom under international human rights standards and disclosure orders are permitted only under stringent conditions.Ricardo Gutiérrez, the general secretary of the European Federation of Journalists, representing over 320,000 journalists, said: “These threats constitute a blatant act of intimidation against journalists who have simply been doing their job, in strict accordance with ethical standards and in the public interest. I am not surprised by this outburst, which confirms that this regime is prepared to do anything to cover up its crimes against humanity and the ongoing genocide in Gaza.”A Guardian spokesperson said: “After first threatening to strip NAZA’s directors of their Israeli citizenship, the Israeli government is now calling for an investigation into their journalistic sources. These moves are all attempts to distract from the urgent questions the film asks about the mass killings of Palestinian civilians in Gaza. Journalists should be free to pursue public interest investigations without threats or harassment.”View image in fullscreenGraffiti depicting Abraham and Szor, and the word ‘traitors’ in Hebrew, appeared on a wall in Ashdod, southern Israel, after NAZA was awarded the special jury prize at the Venice film festival.Photograph: Amir Cohen/ReutersNAZA builds on revelations first published by the Israeli-Palestinian publication +972 Magazine, the Hebrew-language outlet Local Call and the Guardian between 2023 and 2025. Earlier this month, a Guardian spokesperson said the “process of assessing the credibility of the testimonies was rigorous. It included leaked classified documents, detailed verification of specific strikes and corroboration via a wider pool of confidential journalistic sources who did not appear on camera in the film.”In the past three years the team behind the film has “interviewed more than 100 sourcesfamiliar with IDF systems used in the war in Gaza, including senior-ranking commanders directly involved in the authorisation of strikes”, the Guardian spokesperson added.In recent days, the Israeli governmenthas promoted an online film projectthat mimics the style of NAZA, in an attempt to challenge the real film’s findings. Ariel Averbuch, an Israeli attorney and army reservist who made NAZA: The Real Story, described it as an “offensive move” intended to shift the world’s focus from allegations about the Israeli military’s killing of civilians.Film industry heavyweights across the globe, including the heads of the Locarno film festival,have expressed solidarity with Abraham and Szor, saying they stood “firmly in support of film-makers’ rights to pursue difficult and urgent subjects without fear of reprisal”.Explore more on these topicsNAZAIsraelMiddle East and north AfricaBenjamin NetanyahuPalestinePress freedomHuman rightsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Ilhan Omar says she will not be silenced after federal agents raid her home | Trump administration | The Guardian
description: Trump and key allies have accused Omar of immigration fraud, and have called to expel her from the country
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Trump and key allies have accused Omar of immigration fraud, and have called to expel her from the country
Content: Representative Ilhan Omar, Democrat of Minnesota, listens during a Congressional spotlight hearing on Capitol Hill, on 22 September 2026, in Washington.Photograph: Mark Schiefelbein/APView image in fullscreenRepresentative Ilhan Omar, Democrat of Minnesota, listens during a Congressional spotlight hearing on Capitol Hill, on 22 September 2026, in Washington.Photograph: Mark Schiefelbein/APTrump administrationIlhan Omar says she will not be silenced after federal agents raid her homeTrump and key allies have accused Omar of immigration fraud, and have called to expel her from the countryMatt ShuhamMon 12 Oct 2026 12.20 EDTFirst published on Mon 12 Oct 2026 08.50 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFederal agentssearchedRepresentativeIlhan Omar’s home on Monday morning as part of a criminal investigation, according to the Department of Justice andreports inthe Associated Press and Fox News.In a social media post later on Monday, Omarcriticizedthe raid as an attempt by the Trump administration “to target political enemies and weaponize law enforcement” and said she would “not be silenced”.A video posted by Fox showed what appeared to be law enforcement in HSI jackets at what Fox News said was Omar’sWashington DCresidence.“Today in the Washington DC area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice. This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation,” a DoJ spokesperson said.It was unclear what the nature of the warrant was. Omar’s office did not respond to a request for comment, and the White House and Department of Homeland Security referred comment to DoJ. Citing two unnamed sources “close to the investigation”, Fox News reported that the search was related to a criminal fraud investigation concerning Omar’s immigration paperwork, which her late father filled out when she was a child.View image in fullscreenHSI agents outside the residence of  Representative Ilhan Omar in Washington DC on Monday.Photograph: Annabelle Gordon/ReutersDonald Trumpand key allies have accused Omar of fraud related to her family’s immigration history,fantasizing openlyabout denaturalizing her and expelling her from the country.When asked about the raid on Monday, Trump said he had “nothing to do with it” and the investigation is “up to the DoJ”.“I understand they’re looking at her very carefully,” Trump told reporters. “I’ve always found her to be totally crooked, personally, but that has nothing to do with me.”Democrats rebuke federal raid of Ilhan Omar’s home: ‘rogue abuse of power’Read moreThe congresswoman has consistently denied the accusations, though Trump has repeatedly made them national news with gratuitous attacks against Omar, who along with Representative Rashida Tlaib became the United States’s first Muslim congresswoman in 2019.But even amid a presidency known for political andlegalretributionagainst his critics, the search of Omar’s DC home just three weeks before a crucial midterm election day will surely lead to new accusations that Trump was using the government for his own political ends.Administration officials, and the president himself, have long hinted at a federal investigation into Omar. “Let’s see what happens,” Trump said at arallyon Saturday after attacking Omar by name, adding that Vice-President JD Vance “and our people are looking at it very strongly”.It was just the latest in months of talk about investigating Omar. Trump in Decemberaccusedher of having “married her brother” and said she “should be thrown the hell out of our country”, a reference to a years-old but unsubstantiated claim that Omar sought to help her ex-husband – who they allege is really her brother – obtain immigration papers via a sham marriage.Days later, his “border czar” Tom Homansaid: “We’re pulling the records now,” referring to Omar, and said a fraud investigator in Homeland Security Investigations, the ICE division that historically has been tasked with investigative work, would look into the matter.View image in fullscreenHomeland security officers carry boxes from the Washington residence of Ilhan Omar as yellow cordon tape can be seen in the distance.Photograph: J Scott Applewhite/APIn March , Vancetoldrightwing media personality Benny Johnson: “We actually think that Ilhan Omar definitely committed immigration fraud” and that he had recently spoken to top Trump aide Stephen Miller about “what the remedies are”. Homeland security secretary Markwayne MullintoldJohnson last month that there was an ongoing investigation and “something’s going to happen”.“We know that she married her brother to try to bring him into the United States,” Mullin said. “We know he lives now in London. We feel that there may be more to this, the whole family migration, and possibly some illegal activity for them to come to the United States to begin with. But all of us, we’re investigating.”Soon after, Homansaidhe could not “comment on an ongoing criminal investigation.“We’ll let HSI, Homeland Security Investigations continue to do their investigation,” he added.Omar’s social media post after the raid on Monday said: “I’m OK. Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement.”The congresswoman also said Trump had spent years targeting her “with baseless lies and smear campaigns”.“This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced.”Omar has for yearsdeniedunsubstantiatedrumorsfrom Trump and others about herself and her family, including the accusation that her ex-husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, is in fact her brother, and that the marriage was part of an effort to earn him immigration status. Marriage fraud is a felony, though it has a five-year statute of limitations. Omar and Elmiformally divorcedin 2017 after separating in a religious divorce years earlier.View image in fullscreenOfficers during an investigation at the residence of Ilhan Omar on Monday.Photograph: J Scott Applewhite/APThe New York Post last month alsoquotedan unnamed “top immigration official” who said “the Trump administration could initiate a denaturalization process” against Omar if there is sufficient evidence that she or her father lied on immigration applications. The story noted accusations that Omar was older than her recorded age of 17 when she was naturalized, which could be relevant because she received citizenship via her parents. The report also raised questions about Omar’s father, who reportedly claimed to be an educator, though his obituary laterdescribeda military career.As the most prominent Somali-American in the United States, Omar has facedyears of racist attacksfrom the president and his supporters.At his rally Saturday, Trump said of Somalia: “All they have is crime and squalor” and suggested that “our” US constitution did not belong to Omar. Two days earlier, he had written that Minnesota “is being taken over by Somali Immigrants”, even though thevast majorityof Somali-Americans in the state are US citizens.“The Somalians should not be allowed to get away with what they are doing,” Trump wrote, urging supporters in the state to “fight back!”Somali-Americans, especially, have borne relentless insult from the White House in Trump’s second term. In December, the president referred to them as “garbage” who “come from hell, and they complain, and do nothing but bitch”.“Let them go back to where they came from and fix it,” he added.Explore more on these topicsTrump administrationIlhan OmarDonald TrumpMinnesotaWashington DCUS politicsUS CongressnewsShareReuse this content

title: Ministers preparing to slash heat pump subsidies to fund defence spending | Heat pumps | The Guardian
description: Exclusive: Some of £2bn savings needed from energy budget expected to come from boiler upgrade scheme, sources say
Author: Kiran Stacey
Headline: Exclusive: Some of £2bn savings needed from energy budget expected to come from boiler upgrade scheme, sources say
Content: The scheme provides grants of up to £9,000 and has helped tens of thousands of households to install an electric heat pump in place of a gas boiler.Photograph: Andrew Aitchison/In Pictures/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe scheme provides grants of up to £9,000 and has helped tens of thousands of households to install an electric heat pump in place of a gas boiler.Photograph: Andrew Aitchison/In Pictures/Getty ImagesHeat pumpsMinisters preparing to slash heat pump subsidies to fund defence spendingExclusive: Some of £2bn savings needed from energy budget expected to come from boiler upgrade scheme, sources sayKiran StaceyPolicy editorMon 12 Oct 2026 01.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 12 Oct 2026 08.18 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMinisters are preparing to slash the amount of money available to subsidise heat pumps as they look for ways to fund higher defence spending, sources have told the Guardian.Miatta Fahnbulleh, the energy secretary, has been tasked with finding more than £2bn in savings from her budget to help pay for defence investment under a plan drawn up by the previous government.Sources say a portion of those savings will come from cutting the boiler upgrade scheme (BUS) forEnglandand Wales, which provides grants of up to £9,000 to help households switch to cleaner heating methods. The programme will not be abolished altogether but sources say hundreds of millions of pounds will be cut from its £2.7bn budget.The scheme has helped tens of thousands of households install an electric heat pump in place of an old gas boiler, but Treasury officials have long considered it a subsidy used mainly by middle-class households.View image in fullscreenMinisters are expected to give the go-ahead to the Jackdaw gasfield as soon as this week.Photograph: Murdo MacLeod/The GuardianCritics say cutting the scheme woulddamage the nascent British heat pump industryand further undermine the government’s commitment to tackling the climate crisis. Ministers are also expected to give the go-ahead for the Jackdaw gasfield as soon as this week.Madeleine Gabriel, a director at the charity Nesta, said: “Bills are soaring again because of high gas prices. Our reliance on gas is the reason we are in an energy crisis, so cutting funding for heat pumps makes no sense.“It’s a kick in the teeth for the businesses and tradespeople who’ve put in time and money to build the industry.”View image in fullscreenInstallers carrying a heat pump into a residential property for installation in Farnham, Surrey.Photograph: Justin Tallis/AFP/Getty ImagesGreg Jackson, the chief executive of OctopusEnergy, said: “The boiler upgrade scheme is doing exactly what it was meant to do. It’s kicking off an industry to drive down the costs of heat pumps – they can now cost the same to install as a gas boiler after the grant.”He added: “Just as EVs are becoming the new normal, heat pumps are too. In the last 18 months, more than 500,000 have asked us for a quote.“The market is taking off. Cutting the engine now would be brutally damaging.Heat pumpsare undoubtedly our energy future – slashing the cost of living and insulating us against fossil fuel costs and global dictators.”View image in fullscreenMiatta Fahnbulleh, the energy secretary, has to find £2bn of savings from her department’s budget.Photograph: Temilade Adelaja/ReutersA spokesperson for the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero said: “Savings for the defence investment plan (Dip) are a small part of [the department’s] overall budget, which saw a significant uplift at spending review.“We will set out how we will fund essential investment in our national security this autumn.”The overall cuts were agreed to by the former energy secretary, Ed Miliband, as the then prime minister, Keir Starmer, looked for ways to fund a £15bn rise in defence spending over four years. Miliband agreed that the energy department would cut its capital budget by £2bn to help pay for the Dip.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every daySign up toHeadlines UKGet the day’s headlines and highlights emailed direct to you every morningEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion‘It’s been a revelation’: how heat pumps can cool your home in a heatwaveRead moreEnergy officials say the cuts pale in comparison with the overall growth in the energy department’s capital budget, which is one of the fastest growing in Whitehall.The chancellor, John Healey, resigned as defence secretary in June under Starmer, arguing that the defence uplift was not enough. He now has to find an additional £4.7bn in savings over a four-year period beyond what departments have already agreed.Bloombergreported this monththat as part of the cuts to the energy department, ministers were planning to reduce spending on carbon capture and storage (CCS) and green hydrogen schemes.View image in fullscreenThe overall cuts were agreed to by the former energy secretary, Ed Miliband, as the then prime minister Keir Starmer looked for ways to fund a £15bn rise in defence spending over four years.Photograph: Toby Melville/PAThe government had been planning to spend £21.7bn on CCS from now until 2050 as ministers look to make the UK a leader in the still-developing technology.CCS supporters say it is the best way to cut carbon emissions while still protecting Britain’s North Sea oil industry.But its critics say thetechnology is being promoted by fossil fuel companieswho are not being honest about how much it will end up costing the country.Asked recently about the future of the CCS programme, Martin McCluskey, an energy minister, told Politico: “I’m not betraying any confidences when I say that we are having to make some difficult decisions because of what happened as a result of the defence investment plan.”The Guardian has learned that heat pump subsidies are one of the other significant schemes due to be raided to fund the increase in defence spending.The scheme, which offers £7,500 as a basic grant towards an electric heat pump, hassubsidised nearly 80,000heat pumps since it began in 2022. Some properties that are off the grid can claim as much as £9,000 to upgrade.However, given those subsidies cover only just over half the cost of the median heat pump, much of that money has gone to better-off households.The scheme’s supporters say that more than 40% of the money has gone to households with anannual income of below £52,000.But more important, they add, is the fact the subsidies have helped to build a fast-growing domestic heat pump industry, which is expanding by more than 25% a year.Other countries have a far more developed industry.Francesold four times the number of heat pumpsthe UK didlast year.However, the technology also has vocal critics. Dale Vince, the energy entrepreneur and Labour donor,published a report recentlythat said: “Cleaner heat does not yet mean cheaper heat.“Electrifying heat without fixing electricity pricing risks shifting higher costs on to households rather than delivering savings.”Get in touchContact Guardian Politics about this storyThe best public interest journalism relies on first-hand accounts from people in the know. Messages are end to end encrypted and concealed within the routine activity that every Guardian mobile app performs. This prevents an observer from knowing that you are communicating with us at all, let alone what is being said.If you don't already have the Guardian app, download it (iOS/Android) and go to the menu. Scroll down and click onSecure Messaging. When asked who you wish to contact please select thePolitics (UK)team.EmailFor encrypted email correspondence you can create a free Proton Mail account and email us at guardian.politics.desk@protonmail.com.SecureDropIf you can safely use the tor network without being observed or monitored you can send messages and documents to the Guardian via ourSecureDrop platform.Finally, our guide attheguardian.com/tipslists several ways to contact us securely, and discusses the pros and cons of each.Show moreExplore more on these topicsHeat pumpsDefence policyEnergy (Environment)LabourFossil fuelsEnglandWalesnewsShareReuse this content

title: Balkan temperatures swing as heavy rain heads for Greece | Environment | The Guardian
description: Clear skies bring warm days and cold nights to Montenegro, while a low-pressure system moves towards Aegean Sea
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Clear skies bring warm days and cold nights to Montenegro, while a low-pressure system moves towards Aegean Sea
Content: A warm day in Žabljak, Montenegro.Photograph: AlamyView image in fullscreenA warm day in Žabljak, Montenegro.Photograph: AlamyWeather trackerEnvironmentBalkan temperatures swing as heavy rain heads for GreeceClear skies bring warm days and cold nights to Montenegro, while a low-pressure system moves towards Aegean SeaEurope live – latest updatesEd Walton and James Parrish for MetDeskMon 12 Oct 2026 06.48 EDTLast modified on Mon 12 Oct 2026 09.18 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTemperatures fluctuated dramatically in the Balkans last week, with unusually large differences between daytime highs and overnight lows – known as the diurnal range.An area of high pressure over the region brought prolonged sunshine during the day, while clear skies at night allowed temperatures to drop rapidly as heat escaped into the atmosphere without cloud cover to slow the cooling.In Kosanica,Montenegro, the average maximum temperature in October is 15C (59F), while the average minimum is 4C. However, on 4 and 5 October the difference between daytime highs and overnight lows reached 30C, more than double the October average.Elsewhere inEurope, high pressure will build across the north and west over the coming week, pushing an area of low pressure southwards towards the Mediterranean. The low-pressure system will deepen as it crosses the Adriatic and Ionian seas before moving eastwards into the Aegean Sea by the middle of the week.Spells of heavy rain and strong winds are expected to sweep acrossGreeceas a result. Forecast models suggest widespread rainfall of 50-150mm, with the highest totals expected around the island of Skiathos.Towards the end of the week, the system will continue eastwards, bringing showers to parts of Crete, which was hit by severe flooding a week earlier. Those storms swept some cars and trees into the sea.View image in fullscreenPeople cross a bridge over a swollen river as Hurricane Simon approaches Mexico’s Pacific coast in Costalegre, Jalisco state.Photograph: Daniel Becerril/ReutersMeanwhile, Hurricane Simon, a category 4 storm, is moving close to Mexico’s Pacific coast, near the state of Jalisco. It is the latest of 21 named storms in the Pacific this season, 11 of which have reached hurricane strength.At the time of writing, Simon has a central pressure of 933mb and maximum sustained winds of nearly 150mph (241km/h). However, the hurricane is expected to weaken rapidly if its core moves onshore, cutting it off from the warm ocean waters that fuel it.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toDown to EarthThe planet's most important stories. title: Ex-director who oversaw Grenfell cost-cutting leaves council housing role after backlash | Grenfell Tower fire | The Guardian
description: Survivors had criticised ‘outrageous’ appointment of Laura Johnson to £150,000 job with Barnet Group
Author: Jessica Murray
Headline: Survivors had criticised ‘outrageous’ appointment of Laura Johnson to £150,000 job with Barnet Group
Content: The Grenfell Tower memorial wall. Police have asked prosecutors to consider charges including manslaughter and fraud against 54 individuals, and 20 companies and organisations.Photograph: Ben Bauer/PAView image in fullscreenThe Grenfell Tower memorial wall. Police have asked prosecutors to consider charges including manslaughter and fraud against 54 individuals, and 20 companies and organisations.Photograph: Ben Bauer/PAGrenfell Tower fireEx-director who oversaw Grenfell cost-cutting leaves council housing role after backlashSurvivors had criticised ‘outrageous’ appointment of Laura Johnson to £150,000 job with Barnet GroupJessica MurraySocial affairs correspondentMon 12 Oct 2026 05.24 EDTLast modified on Mon 12 Oct 2026 11.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA housing director who oversaw cost cutting at Grenfell Tower before the fatal fire has left a £150,000-a-year senior council housing role after a backlash from bereaved families and survivors.Laura Johnson was the director of housing at the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea (RBKC) at the time of the 2017 Grenfell fire which killed 72 people, and was criticised in the subsequent inquiry for her role in budget-cutting decisions prior to the blaze.It was found that shepushed for a new contractor to carry out the tower’s renovation workson a lower budget, which ultimately meant metal cladding was swapped for combustible plastic-filled panels to save money.In August, she wasappointed the director of development and property at the Barnet Group, which manages the borough’s 13,000 council homes, on a salary of £157,078, a move described by bereaved families and survivors as “outrageous and disrespectful”.In a letter to Joe Powell, the Labour MP for Kensington and Bayswater where Grenfell Tower stood, the company confirmed that Johnson was “no longer employed by The Barnet Group”.Eamon McGoldrick, the chair of the board, said in the letter: “We fully recognise the depth of feeling surrounding the Grenfell Tower tragedy and its continuing impact on bereaved families, survivors, residents and the wider community.“We also fully acknowledge legitimate public interest concerning governance of senior appointments.”He said he could not go into specific details about Johnson’s situation and it is not clear exactly what led to Johnson’s job being terminated.It is understood that Angela Rayner, the housing secretary, wrote to the Barnet Group last month asking for further information about Johnson’s appointment and on what basis it was made.A spokesperson for Grenfell United, which represents survivors and bereaved families, welcomed the news and said it was a “scandal” Johnson had been given the role.“More than nine years after Grenfell, it should not take bereaved families and survivors campaigning for a housing organisation to take the inquiry’s findings seriously,” they said.“But this does not end with Johnson. Others whose conduct was singled out by the Grenfell Tower public inquiry continue to hold positions of authority, have responsibility for health and safety, and draw large salaries.“The inquiry’s findings are there for everyone to read, yet those criticised continue their careers as though nothing has happened. It is an outrage that such damning findings have done nothing to stop them being entrusted with public safety.”‘It’s shaped who we are now’: young people affected by Grenfell fire fight for justice and healingRead morePowell said: “It’s totally inappropriate for any individual criticised by the inquiry to continue to work in housing, particularly while criminal investigations are ongoing. It’s right that Laura Johnson is no longer in such a position.“The Grenfell Tower inquiry was clear about the failings of the RBKC and senior individuals involved in the management of their housing, including the tower.”Last month, a Barnet Group spokesperson insisted Johnson was the “strongest candidate” for the role in a competitive field, and that it had considered her “professional experience, subsequent performance, references, qualifications and overall suitability for the role”.A Barnet Group spokesperson said: “We can confirm that Laura Johnson is no longer employed by The Barnet Group.“In common with any employer, we owe obligations of confidentiality to those working for us, applying for, or being considered for any role at any level. For that reason, it would be inappropriate for us to comment further.”Last month the Metropolitan police said it hadasked prosecutors to consider charges including manslaughter and fraudagainst 54 individuals, and 20 companies and organisations, in relation to the Grenfell fire.The Crown Prosecution Service said charging decisions would be made before the 10th anniversary of the disaster on 14 June 2027.Explore more on these topicsGrenfell Tower fireSocial housingHousingCommunitiesLondonEnglandLocal governmentnewsShareReuse this content

title: Cyber-attack similar to OpenAI Medicare breach seems likely in UK, says minister | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
description: Kanishka Narayan, concerned by Australian incident, says British cyber defences could be bypassed by artificial intelligence agent
Author: Dan Milmo
Headline: Kanishka Narayan, concerned by Australian incident, says British cyber defences could be bypassed by artificial intelligence agent
